title: Cell domains make coordinated group decisions, even random ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cell domains make coordinated group decisions, even random ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cells join into domains that make decisions as a single unit: when left-right asymmetry is randomized in early embryos, a whole domain picks L or R identity rather than individual cells choosing independently, and in frog melanoma-like conversion all melanocytes in a body convert or not together.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Remarkably, however, this randomization is made on a group level – in each case, the entire domain randomly picks L or R identity, not exhibiting a speckled appearance where each cell adopts a stochastic outcome. The decision is random, but all of the cells in the domain are coordinated to make the same random decision (Levin et al., 2002).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin”. Scope: Left-right patterning in early vertebrate embryos; melanocyte conversion in Xenopus tadpoles

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whole-domain concordance versus cell-independent mosaics gives a clear statistical test. Published evidence can test the phenomenon in selected systems, but the decision interpretation and cross-system generalization remain partly confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use spatial single-embryo outcome maps to compare observed within-domain concordance of left-right identity or melanocyte conversion with an independent-cell Bernoulli model, accounting for lineage and shared exposure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shared upstream signals can coordinate outcomes without a domain-level decision process.

Raw spatial cell-level outcomes may not be deposited.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Uniform versus speckled is a direct contrast with independent cell choice, and the claim names the two systems in which it was reported. Those counts exist as published summaries, not as a reanalyzable file, so a binomial test cannot be rerun from raw calls. Xenbase organizes the Xenopus literature and does not replace the missing tables. The pattern can be examined for the published cases and remains confounded with a common upstream bias.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: When left-right identity or melanocyte conversion is randomized, score each embryo as domain-uniform or speckled. Group decision is confirmed if coherent domains predominate over the binomial expectation for independent cells; a speckled mixture at the independent-cell rate would refute coordination.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A shared upstream signal can produce uniform domains without a group decision.

Embryo-by-embryo L/R and pigment scores are not in an open table.

The melanocyte result and the laterality result are different assays.
